# Content Automation Standard

**Version:** 1.0.0  
**Date:** May 2, 2026  
**Status:** Active — applies to all Revvel projects  
**Author:** Audrey Evans (MIDNGHTSAPPHIRE)

---

## 1. Overview

This standard defines how AI-powered content automation is implemented across all Revvel projects. Content Automation eliminates manual content creation bottlenecks by automating the complete pipeline from topic ideation through multi-format publication.

**Key Principle:** Content is generated by AI, refined by AI, but always reviewed by humans before final publication (unless explicitly configured for auto-publish).

---

## 2. Scope

This standard applies to:

- Blog posts and articles
- Video scripts and podcast outlines
- Social media content (Twitter/X threads, LinkedIn posts)
- Email newsletters
- Product documentation
- Marketing copy and landing pages
- Educational content and tutorials

---

## 3. Architecture

### 3.1. Pipeline Stages

Every content generation request flows through these stages:

```text
Input (topic + context)
    ↓
Phase 1: Research & Topic Ideation (2-3 min)
  - AI brainstorms topic variations
  - Validates search demand (optional)
  - Generates content brief
    ↓
Phase 2: Outline Generation (1 min)
  - Structures content sections
  - Defines key points
  - Sets SEO targets
    ↓
Phase 3: Draft Generation (3-4 min)
  - AI writes first complete draft
  - Integrates keywords naturally
  - Adds CTAs and links
    ↓
Phase 4: Content Refinement (2-3 min)
  - Fact-checking pass
  - Tone and pacing improvements
  - Readability optimization
    ↓
Phase 5: Multi-Format Export (1 min)
  - Convert to target formats
  - Generate metadata
  - Run quality gates
    ↓
Output (ready-to-publish content)
```

**Total time: 10-15 minutes** (vs 4-6 hours manually)

---

## 4. Implementation Requirements

### 4.1. Required Components

Every repository implementing content automation must have:

1. **Skill File:** `skills/content-automation/`
   - `SKILL.md` — human-readable documentation
   - `content-automation.skill.yml` — machine-readable config

2. **Workflow:** `.github/workflows/content-automation.yml`
   - Label triggers (`content-automation`, `content`, `writing`, `blog`)
   - Scheduled runs (weekly content calendar generation)
   - Manual dispatch for ad-hoc requests

3. **Script:** `scripts/content-automation.js`
   - Implements all 5 pipeline phases
   - Calls OpenRouter API for AI generation
   - Handles quality gates and output formatting

4. **Output Directory:** `content-automation-output/`
   - Stores generated content
   - Organized by date and slug
   - Git-tracked for version history

### 4.2. Dependencies

- **Node.js** 18+
- **OpenRouter API** account and key
- **GitHub Actions** (built-in)
- **Optional:** TubeBuddy API, VidIQ API (for topic validation)

---

## 5. Configuration

### 5.1. Required Secrets

Set these in repository settings → Secrets and variables → Actions:

| Secret | Purpose | Where to Get It |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | AI content generation | [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys) |

### 5.2. Optional Secrets

| Secret | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `TUBEBUDDY_API_KEY` | YouTube keyword research |
| `VIDIQ_API_KEY` | Video SEO validation |

### 5.3. Repository Variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTENT_TARGET_AUDIENCE` | "general audience" | Who the content is for |
| `CONTENT_BRAND_VOICE` | "professional yet approachable" | Tone guidelines |
| `CONTENT_PRIMARY_KEYWORDS` | "" | Core SEO keywords |
| `CONTENT_AUTO_PUBLISH` | "false" | Skip human review |

---

## 6. AI Model Selection

Content automation uses OpenRouter with model selection optimized per task:

| Task | Model | Rationale | Cost/1k tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Topic ideation & research | `anthropic/claude-opus-4` | Best reasoning, research capability | $15 |
| Content generation (draft) | `deepseek/deepseek-chat` | Cost-effective, good quality | $0.14 |
| Editing & refinement | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` | Excellent editing, tone control | $3 |
| Fact-checking | `openai/gpt-5.4` | Strong verification | $2.50 |

**Cost Example:** A 1500-word blog post uses ~10k tokens total = ~$0.30 per post

---

## 7. Quality Gates

All generated content must pass these automated quality checks:

### 7.1. SEO Quality

- [ ] Title length: 50-60 characters
- [ ] Meta description: 150-160 characters
- [ ] Primary keyword in title
- [ ] Keyword density: 1-2%
- [ ] H2/H3 subheadings present (minimum 3)
- [ ] Internal links included (minimum 2)
- [ ] External authoritative sources (minimum 1)
- [ ] All images have alt text

### 7.2. Readability

- [ ] Flesch reading ease score ≥ 60
- [ ] Average sentence length ≤ 20 words
- [ ] Paragraph length ≤ 150 words
- [ ] Active voice ≥ 80%
- [ ] No unexplained jargon

### 7.3. Content Structure

- [ ] Clear introduction with hook
- [ ] Logical section flow
- [ ] Strong conclusion with CTA
- [ ] Word count within target range
- [ ] No orphaned sections

### 7.4. Technical Quality

- [ ] No broken links
- [ ] Images optimized (< 200KB)
- [ ] Valid markdown/HTML
- [ ] No spelling errors
- [ ] No placeholder text (e.g., "[INSERT X]")

**Pass Threshold:** Content must pass all SEO and Technical gates, and at least 80% of Readability and Structure checks.

---

## 8. Output Structure

Generated content follows this directory structure:

```text
content-automation-output/
└── YYYY-MM-DD-{slug}/
    ├── metadata.json          # Title, keywords, metrics
    ├── brief.md               # Research and topic brief
    ├── outline.md             # Structured outline
    ├── draft_v1.md            # First AI-generated draft
    ├── draft_final.md         # Refined, ready-to-publish
    ├── formats/
    │   ├── blog.html          # Blog-ready HTML
    │   ├── video-script.md    # Timestamped video script
    │   ├── social-thread.md   # Twitter/X thread
    │   ├── linkedin-post.md   # LinkedIn format
    │   └── email.html         # Newsletter-ready HTML
    └── assets/
        ├── cover-image.jpg    # Cover image (manual)
        └── social-card.jpg    # Social preview (manual)
```

**Note:** Images must be added manually or via separate image generation workflow.

## 9. Usage Examples

### 9.1. Generate Blog Post via Issue

1. Create a new issue
2. Set title: "Write blog post about best budget headphones 2026"
3. Add label: `content-automation`
4. Automation triggers within seconds
5. Review generated content in `content-automation-output/`

### 9.2. Generate Video Script via Workflow Dispatch

1. Go to Actions → Content Automation
2. Click "Run workflow"
3. Fill inputs:
   - Topic: "How to file for burial insurance"
   - Format: video
   - Urgency: draft
4. Review output in repository

### 9.3. Weekly Content Calendar (Scheduled)

Every Sunday 09:00 UTC:
- Workflow runs automatically
- Generates 2-4 blog post ideas
- Creates content calendar for next week
- Commits to repository

## 11. Best Practices

### 11.1. For Content Quality

1. **Always fact-check AI output** — AI can hallucinate statistics
2. **Edit for brand voice** — First drafts are generic
3. **Add human insights** — Personal experiences matter
4. **Include visuals** — Text needs images/diagrams
5. **Test CTAs** — Verify links and calls-to-action work

### 11.2. For SEO

1. **Research keywords first** — Don't guess
2. **Internal linking** — Connect existing content
3. **Schema markup** — Add structured data
4. **Mobile preview** — Check mobile readability
5. **Content depth** — Comprehensive > thin content

### 11.3. For Efficiency

1. **Batch content requests** — Generate multiple posts at once
2. **Reuse outlines** — Save successful templates
3. **Update regularly** — Refresh quarterly
4. **Monitor performance** — Track which topics work
5. **Automate distribution** — Hook into noimosai for publishing

---

## 12. Troubleshooting

### Content is too generic
**Solution:** Add more context in brief, specify keywords explicitly, run second refinement pass

### Facts are incorrect
**Solution:** Enable fact-checking gate, add authoritative sources, use GPT-5.4 for verification

### SEO score is low
**Solution:** Run keyword research first, specify primary/secondary keywords, use SEO templates

### Tone doesn't match brand
**Solution:** Update `CONTENT_BRAND_VOICE` variable, include example content in brief

### API rate limit exceeded
**Solution:** Implement exponential backoff, queue requests, use lower-tier models

## 13. Cost Management

### 13.1. Estimated Monthly Costs

Assuming 20 blog posts + 40 social posts + 4 newsletters per month:

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| OpenRouter API | $10-15 |
| TubeBuddy (optional) | $0-9 |
| VidIQ (optional) | $0-7.50 |
| **Total** | **$10-32/month** |

**ROI:** Saves 80-100 hours of manual writing per month (~$2,000-4,000 value at $25/hr)

### 13.2. Cost Optimization

- Use DeepSeek for drafts ($0.14/1k vs $15/1k for Opus)
- Batch API calls to reduce overhead
- Cache common research briefs
- Reuse outlines for similar topics
- Set `max_tokens` limits appropriately

## 14. Metrics & KPIs

Track these metrics to measure content automation effectiveness:

| Metric | Target | How to Measure |
|---|---|---|
| Generation time | < 15 min/piece | Workflow duration |
| Cost per piece | < $0.50 | OpenRouter API costs |
| Quality score | > 70/100 | Internal rubric |
| SEO pass rate | 100% | Automated checks |
| Edit time saved | > 80% | Before/after comparison |
| Publish rate | 10+ pieces/week | GitHub commits |
| Content ROI | > 10x cost | Traffic × value |

## 15. Maintenance

### Weekly
- Review generated content quality
- Update templates based on performance
- Refresh keyword lists

### Monthly
- Audit model selection (cost vs quality)
- Update brand voice guidelines
- Review automation rules

### Quarterly
- Analyze content performance (traffic, engagement)
- Optimize prompts and templates
- Update OpenRouter model selections
- Refresh quality gate criteria

---

## 16. Security & Compliance

### 16.1. Data Privacy

- Never include PII in content generation prompts
- Don't send proprietary data to AI models
- Review generated content for accidental data leaks
- Follow GDPR/CCPA guidelines for user data

### 16.2. API Key Management

- Store API keys in GitHub Secrets only
- Never commit keys to repository
- Rotate keys quarterly
- Monitor usage for anomalies

### 16.3. Content Licensing

- All AI-generated content is owned by the repository owner
- Cite sources appropriately
- Follow fair use guidelines
- Add transparency note ("AI-assisted") where appropriate

---

Before deploying content automation:

- [ ] OpenRouter API key configured in Secrets

- [ ] Quality gates configured appropriately
- [ ] Brand voice guidelines documented
- [ ] Team trained on reviewing AI content
- [ ] Monitoring and metrics tracking in place
